cards.title: Naive loss-style decoupling bound
cards.role: Provides the sufficient qubit-loss comparison and exposes why accessible measurement outcomes can improve the threshold.

checks.reason: The trace-distance exponent and algebraically equivalent criterion are explicit in the main text.
An exponentially vanishing upper bound requires 1-2p-gamma>0, exactly gamma<1-2p.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the base-two exponent over finite N,gamma,p grids; used as a threshold oracle rather than source data.

cards.title: Tight decoupling bound with accessible outcomes

source_refs.value: paper-source/manuscript_supp.tex:571-706; Cauchy-Schwarz, Haar contractions, and final bound

cards.role: Quantifies QEC protection under projective measurements and predicts p_c tending to one in the deep-scrambling large-block limit.

checks.reason: The supplement prints the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, both Haar contractions, and the final exponential bound.
Subtraction cancels the common leading 2^[-(gamma+p)N] and yields the exponent 1-gamma-p after multiplying the Hilbert dimensions.
At gamma=0 the condition permits every p<1; discarding the classical register recovers the weaker loss-style criterion.

cards.numerical_form: Finite-N decoupling exponent and threshold line gamma=1-p, independently evaluated before comparison to entropy trajectories.

cards.title: Unitary frame potential and Haar lower bound
cards.role: Tests when finite-depth random Clifford circuits approximate unitary designs.

checks.reason: Definition, Haar values, and U-dagger-V to depth-(2d-1) reduction are explicit in Supplement S1.
A singleton identity ensemble yields 2^(2nk), demonstrating the expected large non-design value.
For dimension at least k the Haar moments are 1,2,6,24 for k=1..4.

cards.numerical_form: Monte Carlo mean of Q_U^k with Q_U=|Tr U|^2 for depth-(2d-1) composite circuits.

cards.title: Clifford trace from the fixed-Pauli kernel
cards.role: Makes the n=22 frame-potential calculation polynomial instead of constructing an exponential unitary matrix.

checks.reason: Pauli twirl, kernel construction, sign cases, and phase-aware row reduction are explicit in the supplement.
One negative fixed generator pairs every positive fixed Pauli with a negative one, forcing Q_U=0.
The exact dense-trace identity is fully specified as the independent small-system gate before n=22 sampling.

cards.numerical_form: GF(2) nullity plus conjugation-phase consistency, returning an exact integer Q_U for each circuit.

cards.title: Subsystem entropy from supported stabilizers

source_refs.value: paper-source/manuscript_arxiv_03.tex:318-324; stabilizer simulation references and flat entanglement spectrum

cards.role: Turns a stabilizer tableau into every half-chain and multipartition entropy in the numerical figures.

checks.reason: The paper explicitly selects Clifford stabilizer simulation and states the flat entanglement spectrum; the rank formula is the independently derived numerical form.
Tracing the stabilizer projector expansion retains exactly the subgroup supported in A, whose rank fixes the flat reduced-state spectrum.
Product states give zero entropy and a Bell pair cut gives one bit; purity gives S(A)=S(Abar).

cards.numerical_form: Exact GF(2) rank of stabilizer generators restricted to the subsystem complement.

source_refs.value: paper-source/manuscript_supp.tex:244-274; Supp. Fig. S3 caption and discussion

cards.role: Fixes timing, sign, and normalization for the dynamic numerical evidence.

checks.reason: The captions define half-chain normalization and entropy change before/after each measurement layer.
For a pure state 0<=s<=1, while average projective measurements cannot increase the entanglement across a fixed cut under the stated trajectory average.

cards.numerical_form: Two entropy evaluations per time step plus realization mean, standard deviation, and standard error.

cards.title: Half-chain finite-size scaling

source_refs.value: paper-source/manuscript_supp.tex:286-350; scaling ansatz, subtracted form, and cost

cards.role: Generates Supp. Fig. S4 collapses and its depth-dependent exponent estimate.

checks.reason: The supplement states the ansatz, asymptotic branches, variance-weighted cost, two-step optimization, and bootstrap protocol.
The printed asymptotes yield extensive entropy below p_c and size-independent entropy above p_c.

cards.numerical_form: Bounded p_c,nu optimization with overlap-only interpolation, cost surface, and bootstrap samples.
open_questions: The precise interpolation convention in the cited collapse implementation is not repeated; sensitivity must be reported.

cards.title: Tripartite mutual information and scaling

source_refs.value: paper-source/manuscript_supp.tex:354-395; I3 definition, ansatz, and fitted table

cards.role: Provides the cleaner transition crossing and critical exponent used in Supp. Fig. S5 and Table SI.

checks.reason: The supplement defines four periodic partitions, I3, the scaling variable, and the expected O(1) critical behavior.
A product stabilizer state gives zero for every entropy and hence I3=0.

cards.numerical_form: Seven exact subsystem entropies per trajectory, followed by the same bounded collapse machinery.

cards.title: Capacity of a degradable measurement channel

source_refs.value: paper-source/manuscript_supp.tex:440-567; channel dilation through capacity relation

cards.role: Connects the entanglement transition to recoverable coherent quantum information.

checks.reason: The degradable-channel argument, block-diagonal output, coherent information, and final capacity identity are explicit in the main paper and supplement.
The environment has the same diagonal record as M, so tracing S from SM degrades the output to the complementary channel.
For block-diagonal rho_SM, S(SM)=H(p)+sum p_i S(rho_S[i]) and S(M)=H(p), yielding the conditional entropy.

cards.numerical_form: Analytic scientific claim; small channel examples may check the entropy identity but no schematic is rendered as numerical evidence.

cards.title: Logarithmic entropy at criticality

source_refs.value: paper-source/manuscript_supp.tex:428-438; critical entropy and alpha extraction

cards.role: Defines the alpha values in Supp. Fig. S6(c).

checks.reason: The supplement states the critical logarithmic entropy and extracts alpha from sizes through L=64.
Setting p=p_c makes the scaling function a size-independent constant, leaving alpha ln L plus an intercept.

cards.numerical_form: Weighted linear regression of independently simulated S(p_c,L) against ln L.
